decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "The proposed MVP covers saving... bookmarks." Round 1 client: "saving links... That's the heart of what I asked for."
decisions.note: The specification-stage decision supports saving bookmarks and presents no conflict with URL-based saving.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "The proposed MVP covers... editing... bookmarks." Round 1 client generally approves "editing" but neither entry identifies which bookmark fields are editable.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, generic editing is recorded, but the evidence cannot establish whether URL, title, description, tags, and note are all editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "The proposed MVP covers... searching... bookmarks." Round 1 client: "finding them again with search."
decisions.note: The specification-stage basic search decision conforms to full-text search at the level presented; no advanced search behavior is claimed here.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "The proposed MVP covers... tagging." Round 1 client approves organizing with "tags."
decisions.note: The specification includes bookmark tagging with no recorded conflict.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker lists "filtering" separately from "tagging"; Round 1 client likewise approves "tags, and filters" without identifying the filter behavior.
decisions.note: The specification-stage presentation does not establish that selecting a specific tag filters to that tag's bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker presents "archiving, restoring, and deleting bookmarks." Round 1 client approves "archiving, restoring, and deleting."
decisions.note: Archiving is presented as reversible and distinct from deletion, conforming to the recorded archive/delete behavior at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker includes "deleting bookmarks." Round 1 client identifies deleting as part of keeping bookmarks tidy and approves.
decisions.note: Bookmark deletion is included at the specification gate.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "accounts, sharing, imports, extensions, and automatic page metadata are deferred." Round 1 client says "Otherwise this matches what I had in mind. Approved" without mentioning import.
decisions.note: Deferring bookmark import diverges from Netscape HTML import. The client gives only general approval and does not express the import expectation or difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 maker: "automatic page metadata [is] deferred." Round 1 client: "that means when I save a link I'll always have to type the title myself, right? I can live with that for a first version" and wants automatic title filling later.
decisions.note: At the specification gate, the client explicitly identifies the missing automatic title behavior and accepts its deferral.

decisions.evidence: Round 1 client asks whether a title must always be typed. Round 2 maker resolves it: "User-entered titles remain required." Round 2 client: "titles are still typed by hand... that's fine for this version."
decisions.note: The linked clarification is counted once at its plan-stage disposition. Requiring a manually entered title means entering a URL alone is insufficient, but the client explicitly accepts that departure.

decisions.evidence: Round 2 maker: "automatic page information is still deferred." Round 2 client: "automatic page info is deferred — that's fine for this version, as we agreed."
decisions.note: The plan-stage presentation repeats the metadata departure, and the client explicitly recognizes and accepts it.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker describes "13 tasks for saving and revisiting bookmarks" and an MVP covering "saving, persistence, reopening." Round 3 client approves the task breakdown.
decisions.note: The task-stage decision continues to support saving bookmarks.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker describes tasks for "saving and revisiting bookmarks" and "reopening." Round 3 client approves the breakdown.
decisions.note: Revisiting or reopening saved bookmarks conforms to navigating back to their original links at the level presented.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker includes "maintenance, archiving, restoring, and deletion" tasks. Round 3 client approves the task list.
decisions.note: The task-stage presentation retains deletion and a reversible archive flow distinct from deletion.

decisions.evidence: Round 3 maker says the MVP includes "duplicate handling." Round 3 client approves without asking what that handling does.
decisions.note: At the task gate, the record does not yet establish whether duplicates are prevented and directed to editing the existing bookmark.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: "Save links with manually entered titles." Round 4 client: "typing titles by hand and having the app fill them in automatically is something to look at in a future version, but it doesn't hold anything back here."
decisions.note: At implementation review, manual title entry remains the substitute for URL-only saving with automatic title collection. The client explicitly identifies and accepts the difference.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker implements saving links with "notes." Round 4 client says they saved a link with "notes," but neither entry mentions Markdown authoring or rendered Markdown.
decisions.note: Implementation review establishes note storage but cannot establish conformity or divergence for Markdown rendering.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker: "Save links with... tags." Round 4 client reports saving a link with tags.
decisions.note: The implemented bookmark-tag assignment conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists "Search." Round 4 client reports finding the bookmark again by searching.
decisions.note: Basic implemented search conforms to the presented full-text-search decision; no decision about advanced query syntax is recorded.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker explicitly lists "tag filtering." Round 4 client reports that they "filtered by tag."
decisions.note: The implementation-stage tag-filter decision conforms.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents "four sort modes." Round 4 client accepts the application.
decisions.note: Multiple implemented sort modes conform to sortable bookmark lists.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker lists "Editing" among implemented behavior. Round 4 client broadly accepts the app but does not identify editable fields.
decisions.note: Implementation review does not establish whether every required field—especially URL and description—is editable.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker implements "archiving, restoring." Round 4 client reports: "Archiving pulled it out of my main list but kept it safe in the archive, restoring brought it back intact."
decisions.note: The maker presents archive/restore behavior consistent with hiding content without deleting it and allowing reversal.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker implements "confirmed permanent deletion." Round 4 client reports that permanent deletion "took a deliberate step."
decisions.note: Permanent deletion is available and explicitly distinguished from reversible archiving.

decisions.evidence: Round 4 maker presents "Duplicate-address warnings." Round 4 client praises receiving "a clear warning when I tried to save the same address twice" and generally accepts the app, but never states the reference expectation of being guided to edit the existing bookmark.
decisions.note: At implementation review, a warning is presented in place of the specified convergence to editing the existing bookmark. The client's praise and approval do not explicitly identify that difference, so they are not an accepted divergence.
